thread.title: With deferred liabilities, Verizon will get earnings benefit from tax bill

author: Francine McKenna
title: With deferred liabilities, Verizon will get earnings benefit from tax bill
text:
Verizon Communications joins a lucky group of companies with primarily good news to share about the impact of the Tax Cut and Jobs Act law, signed by President Trump at the end of December.
Verizon VZ, +2.43% reports significant deferred tax liabilities, so the telecommunications company reported to the Securities and Exchange Commission on Wednesday that it would record a big positive impact from the new law—a $16.8 billion one-time reduction in its net deferred income tax liabilities—which is expected to drop directly to its bottom line and pump up earnings per share by approximately $4.10.
Verizon is expected to formally report fourth-quarter 2017 earnings on Tuesday.
A slew of companies like IBM IBM, -0.13% , Citigroup C, +0.04% and General Motors GM, +0.32% are delivering bad news earnings reports, instead, because they have large deferred tax assets that lost value with the corporate tax rate reduction from 35% to 21%, and prompted multibillion dollar earnings hits in addition to a potential negative impact from the one-time penalty tax on any accumulated overseas earnings.
Read: Tax bill lowered corporate tax rate, so why are some companies announcing charges? 
Also: These companies will take a huge profit hit from lower tax rates 
But companies with net deferred liabilities will calculate a positive impact for the change in tax rates, because what they eventually pay is now calculated based on a 21% rate versus a 35% corporate tax rate. That is not including any additional cost for the tax on overseas earnings. 
Wells Fargo & Co WFC, +0.43% is the only big bank so far to see its fourth-quarter profit get a boost from writing down its deferred tax liabilities to reflect the lower rate. The bank said its income of $6.15 billion, or $1.16 a share, benefited from a $3.35 billion one-time tax boost. 
Coming up there may be a boost to earnings at Berkshire Hathaway BRK.B, +0.80% and its subsidiary BNSF Railway, telecommunications companies such as AT&T Inc T, +1.44% , Comcast CMCSA, +0.52% and wholly owned subsidiary NBCUniversal Media LLC, and Charter Communications CHTR, +0.71% , as well as Kraft Heinz KHC, +0.36% , Apple AAPL, -0.92% , Pfizer Inc PFE, -0.38% , and Exxon Mobil XOM, +0.93% . These are the companies with the largest net deferred tax liability balances as of the end of 2016. 
Generally accepted accounting principles, the rules companies that list on U.S. stock exchanges must follow when preparing financial statements for the public, require companies to record the impact on deferred income taxes of any tax law change in the quarter that the new law change is enacted, in this case for periods that include December 2017. The SEC issued guidelines the day the law was passed, Dec. 22, that allow companies to estimate the impact on earnings for the fourth quarter and year ending Dec. 31, 2017.
Verizon said the change will not have any impact on 2017 cash flows. In addition, the company said in the filing with the SEC it did not estimate any material impacts from the new overseas profit one-time repatriation tax or its implementation of the new territorial tax system. H
Verizon also signaled in the filing that it would see a positive impact from its implementation of new rules for accounting for the recognition of revenues. Verizon plans to reflect a pretax increase of $4 billion to $4.6 billion as the cumulative effect of the changes on prior period results— primarily in the way it accounts for new wireless subsidy contracts and future commission costs incurred by its wireless and wireline businesses—to its 2018 opening retained earnings balance. Wireless subsidy contracts currently represent approximately 20% of Verizon’s total postpaid wireless phone base and are primarily business customers.
Under the old rules, equipment revenue for subsidy contracts was required to be limited to the amount of received when equipment was delivered. Under the new rules, called ASC 606, Verizon is required to allocate the total contract revenue to the various contract components such as equipment and service. As a result, it expects to recognize more equipment revenue when it is delivered, and less service revenue over the contract term than in the past.

Also, on an ongoing basis, a significant amount of commission costs which would have historically been expensed as incurred under our previous rules, will now be deferred and written off typically over the contract term. Verizon said the overall effect on total revenues will be “insignificant” but total expenses will be reduced by $900 million to $1.2 billion. Prior period results will not be restated for comparison purposes.
